extracted.intended_audience: general readers / historians / readers of Andrew Carnegie's autobiography; those seeking historical examples of self-improvement and philanthropy
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from Andrew Carnegie's autobiography recounting his youth as a working boy, early jobs (bobbin factory, telegraph messenger), self-education, and influences that shaped his views on libraries, thrift, and advancement. Contains life-maxims and implicit advice about personal development and philanthropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize opportunity promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is a great mistake not to seize the opportunity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to accept a trial and to 'stay there if I could' when given a chance; Carnegie's immediate readiness to begin work for Mr. Brooks led directly to his career break. Example: when offered the messenger position he volunteered to start at once rather than risk losing the chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseverance / never give up
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie emphasizes endurance and persistence: 'Of one thing I was sure, he ought never to give up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persist despite difficult, unpleasant, or humiliating tasks (e.g., running an engine, bathing spools in oil that produced nausea). Persistence is portrayed as a moral duty and practical path to future change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of formal and self-education
rubrics_metrics.description: Education (formal and self-directed) is essential: Scotland required schooling; Carnegie studied double-entry bookkeeping at night school and read voraciously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue learning in spare time (night school, Colonel Anderson's library); practical skills like bookkeeping materially advance prospects. 'Youths must acquire knowledge themselves.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public libraries are high-return philanthropy
rubrics_metrics.description: "There was no use to which money could be applied so productive of good ... as the founding of a public library."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide broad access to books—opening a library to working boys yields disproportionate social benefit. Carnegie uses his experience with Colonel Anderson's open library as rationale for later library philanthropy and as evidence of long-term impact on youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start at the bottom and learn all parts of the business
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with humble tasks and learn by doing (sweeping the office, firing boilers, bathing spools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early willingness to do lowly tasks builds practical knowledge and credibility; many prominent men and future leaders began by sweeping offices. Example: messenger boys swept and practiced on instruments, which led to telegraphy skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate practice and skill-building in spare moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use every spare minute to practice useful skills (memorizing firm names and addresses; practicing telegraphy by ear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic, small-scale exercises (calling off firms, practicing Morse by ear, playing with the telegraph key) rapidly improve competence and create opportunities to demonstrate ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know people and cultivate practical networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity with business houses and their people gives messengers advantage and saves effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn who the men and employees are, cultivate cordial relations; personal recognition often yields compliments and easier deliveries — networking as practical efficiency and advancement tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrift and transparent family finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful saving and family budgeting matter: 'Every penny that I could save I knew was needed at home.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparency in household finances (mother as treasurer) and prioritize debt repayment; small regular savings can discharge significant obligations and change family status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and simple financial organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Pooling small extra earnings (the 'dime messages') and dividing them equally resolved conflicts and is described as 'my first essay in financial organization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple cooperative arrangements to manage irregular small incomes; appoint roles (treasurer) and set clear rules to preserve harmony and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt appearance and comportment to occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Present oneself smartly to improve prospects (Carnegie wore his 'one white linen shirt' and 'whole Sunday suit' to interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful dress and bearing can influence impressions in interviews or public interactions; modest means should not prevent making an effort to appear fit for opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural exposure cultivates higher tastes and imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Theater, literature, and music broaden horizons and inspire: Shakespeare and Wagner opened new worlds to Carnegie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out dramatic and musical experiences when possible; early exposure (theater privileges for telegraph staff, choir practice) can spark enduring intellectual and aesthetic appetites that enrich life and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of mentors and benefactors
rubrics_metrics.description: Generous patrons and kind employers (Colonel Anderson, Mr. Hay, Mr. Brooks) materially affect young lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and value mentorship and institutional generosity; such acts (opening a library, offering kinder duties, allowing trials) provide access and create lasting gratitude — Carnegie later memorialized benefactors and replicated the generosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical competence and trustworthiness win promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Being competent and careful (watching the office, handling messages) leads to increased pay and responsibility (Glass raised his wage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate reliability in small entrusted tasks; supervisors reward evident worth with promotion and pay increases. Example: taking responsibility in the manager's absence and successfully handling an important message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small things and trifles can have large consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: "A word, a look, an accent, may affect the destiny not only of individuals, but of nations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss minor actions or moments as unimportant; attention to small details and moments of chance interactions can redirect careers and lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative in conflict resolution and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposing practical solutions (pooling dime messages) and taking leadership roles (treasurer) shows early administrative ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disputes arise among peers, propose fair, enforceable solutions and accept responsibilities; such initiatives demonstrate character and capacity for organization.
